openai/gpt-5.6-sol#pass2.title: CRC-16-CCITT starts at 0x0000 instead of the required 0xFFFF, making encoded frames incompatible with conforming peers.
MAX_PAYLOAD is 65536, so encode and parse admit one byte beyond the 65535-byte contract limit.
Public consume accepts counts larger than the available data, allowing unread bytes to be discarded or cursor arithmetic to overflow.
Repeated next_frame use with a persistent partial suffix advances the cursor without compacting, allowing the backing vector to grow without bound despite HIGH_WATER.
next_frame slices the declared payload and trailer without first checking that the complete frame is buffered, so a partial frame can panic.
A checksum failure consumes the entire declared frame instead of resynchronizing at the next magic sequence, potentially discarding a recoverable frame.
A checksum mismatch is returned as Ok(None), silently dropping malformed input instead of surfacing FrameError.
The drain budget can underflow after a corrupt prefix and reentrant feed cause more frame bytes to be consumed than remain in the snapshot budget.
drain discards every parsing error and exposes no return channel, violating the requirement that malformed frames surface FrameError.
Resynchronization drops a trailing 0xA5 byte that could combine with the next feed's 0x5A, destroying a magic sequence split across chunks.
